steps.say: This muscle cancer of childhood is striking twice, in toddlers and again in teenagers. Rhabdomyosarcoma is an embryonic skeletal muscle cancer causing 4 percent of paediatric malignancy with bimodal peak at 2 to 5 years and 15 to 19 years. Children with neurofibromatosis type 1, Li Fraumeni and Beckwith Wiedemann syndromes carry a higher cancer predisposition.
steps.tx: **Rhabdomyosarcoma** (muscle lineage childhood cancer) is an embryonic skeletal muscle cancer causing **4** percent of paediatric malignancy with **bimodal peak** (twin age hump) at **2** to **5** years and **15** to **19** years, enriched in neurofibromatosis type 1, Li Fraumeni and Beckwith Wiedemann **cancer predisposition** (inherited risk) syndromes.

steps.say: Most tumours are the friendly embryonal kind, while the alveolar pattern warns of trouble. Embryonal including botryoid and spindle forms exceeds two thirds and behaves best, alveolar behaves worst, and pleomorphic sits intermediate. Muscle proteins myosin, actin, desmin and myoglobin confirm lineage on immunohistochemistry.
steps.tx: **Embryonal** (primitive muscle) including botryoid and spindle forms exceeds two thirds and behaves best, **alveolar** (nest pattern) behaves worst, pleomorphic sits intermediate, and muscle proteins myosin, actin, desmin and myoglobin confirm lineage on **immunohistochemistry** (stain profiling). Desmin and myogenin stains confirm the diagnosis on tiny needle cores.

vis.alt: Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma with botryoid grapes, cambium layer and strap cells beside alveolar nests with fibrous septa and giant cells.
vis.caption: Embryonal botryoid disease behaves best; alveolar nests with PAX3-FOXO1 behave worst. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Head and neck lumps lead the list, but bleeding from bladder or vagina tells the same story elsewhere. Head and neck leads at 35 percent then genitourinary 25 percent then extremities 20 percent. Orbital proptosis with visual loss, parameningeal headache with bloody nasal discharge, bladder trigone hematuria with obstruction, vaginal grape like botryoid masses, and paratesticular painless scrotal swelling complete the map.
steps.tx: Head and neck leads at **35** percent then genitourinary **25** percent then extremities **20** percent, with orbital proptosis and visual loss, **parameningeal** (skull base) headache with bloody nasal discharge, bladder trigone hematuria with obstruction, vaginal grape like **botryoid** (bunch of grapes) masses, and **paratesticular** (beside testis) painless scrotal swelling.

vis.alt: Six scrotal swellings with comparison table contrasting hydrocele, varicocele, hernia, cyst, tumour and torsion features.
vis.caption: Painless paratesticular swelling needs tumour in the differential; transillumination and impulse separate mimics. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: No blood test finds this tumour, so tissue under the microscope remains mandatory. No serum marker exists, imaging maps encasement, nodes and metastases, and incisional or core needle biopsy is mandatory since aggressive upfront resection is unnecessary for this chemosensitive and radiosensitive tumour.
steps.tx: No serum marker exists, imaging maps encasement, nodes and metastases, and incisional or **core needle biopsy** (tissue sampling) is mandatory since aggressive upfront resection is unnecessary for this **chemosensitive** (drug responsive) and **radiosensitive** (radiation responsive) tumour. Wide excision is avoided at diagnosis to preserve function for later.

steps.say: Chemotherapy leads and surgery follows, with radiation cleaning up what remains. Biopsy then risk based VAC chemotherapy is the preferred path, radiation controls microscopic residual and unresectable disease, and vincristine with dactinomycin covers low risk subgroup A with cyclophosphamide added for higher risk.
steps.tx: Biopsy then **risk stratification** (group based intensity) with **VAC chemotherapy** (vincristine, dactinomycin, cyclophosphamide) is the preferred path, **radiation therapy** (focused beams) controls microscopic residual and unresectable disease, and vincristine with dactinomycin covers low risk subgroup A with cyclophosphamide added for higher risk.

steps.say: Surgeons and oncologists speak one language through the grouping system. Clinical grouping runs I fully resected, II grossly resected with microscopic or nodal disease, III gross residual or biopsy only, IV distant metastases at diagnosis. TNM staging with resection margins refines prognosis beside the group.
steps.tx: **Clinical grouping** (surgical result language) runs I fully resected, II grossly resected with microscopic or nodal disease, III gross residual or biopsy only, IV distant metastases at diagnosis, and **TNM staging** (tumour node metastasis) with **resection margins** (cut edge status) refines prognosis.

steps.say: Low risk disease is nearly always curable, while high risk and relapse remain sobering. Three year failure free survival is 88 percent low risk, 55 to 76 percent intermediate and under 30 percent high risk, with 15 percent metastatic at diagnosis and 30 percent suffering relapse with only 17 percent five year survival.
steps.tx: Three year **failure free survival** (cure without events) is **88** percent low risk, **55** to **76** percent intermediate and under **30** percent high risk, with **15** percent showing **metastatic disease** (spread) at diagnosis and **30** percent suffering **relapse** (return) with only **17** percent five year survival.

steps.say: Limbs are cut widely with nodes mapped, bladders are saved where possible, and boys keep careful follow up. Extremity lesions need wide local excision with sentinel node mapping and usually radiation for alveolar histology, bladder prostate primaries prioritise bladder preservation with preoperative chemoradiation, and paratesticular disease needs radical inguinal orchiectomy with retroperitoneal dissection under 10 years.
steps.tx: Extremity lesions need **wide local excision** (generous removal) with sentinel node mapping and usually radiation for alveolar histology, bladder prostate primaries prioritise **bladder preservation** (organ sparing) with preoperative chemoradiation, and paratesticular disease needs radical inguinal orchiectomy with **retroperitoneal dissection** (node clearance) under **10** years.
